evidence.claim: Tie counts reproduce exactly. On confirmation (ef_st_all vs ef_a3_rl_pr): 44b6 has 11 wins, 1 loss and 59 exact ties (the loss is 44b6_ddf577ad, -0.00122, +1 FP), mean +0.00106. 6bba has 46 wins, 0 losses and 18 ties, mean +0.00274. Per-video sign test, one-sided: p = 0.0032 on 44b6 and 1.4e-14 on 6bba.
evidence.source: recomputed from experiments/l2_daughternet/edge_anatomy/l6_per_video_confirmation_vs_ef.csv (the hypothesis's l6_stitch/per_video_confirmation.csv does not exist under that name)

evidence.claim: The ties come from label coverage, not from no-ops. 47 of the 59 tied 44b6 videos did add stitched edges, and none of them was evaluable. Node counts are identical in all 135 videos. Evaluable added edges on confirmation: +168 TP / +9 FP (precision 0.949).
evidence.source: same CSV, stitch_added and num_pred_nodes columns

evidence.claim: 44b6 videos are overlapping crops, so they are not independent. The 12 non-tied 44b6 videos fall into only 5 leak groups (sizes 3, 3 with the loss, 2, 2, 2). By cluster (group mean), 44b6 is 5 wins / 0 losses / 13 ties over 18 clusters, one-sided sign p = 0.031. That is still significant but about 10x weaker than the p ~0.003 claimed.

Dropping zero differences is the standard sign test (Dixon & Mood 1946): 'pairs are omitted for which there is no difference'. A win rate over ALL videos, ties included, is not a valid sign statistic when most differences are zero by construction. Other tie procedures exist (Coakley & Heise: modified or trinomial tests when many zeros are expected).

Two-stage linking has literature precedent: frame-to-frame linking first, then linking track-segment ends to starts to close gaps (Jaqaman 2008 LAP; TrackMate's segment-linking step, where the no-link alternative cost is 1.05 x max cost). Re-adding the linker's own end->start edges after the relink is a restricted form of that second step.

st_p07, the hypothesis's shipping form, FAILS the existing per-embryo mean gate. Confirmation 44b6 delta: st_p07 +0.00078, st_p08 +0.00073, st_p06 +0.00102, st_all/st_p05 +0.00117; the gate is >= +0.001. The p<0.7 slice is 41 TP / 11 FP (0.79), still well above break-even. st_all is the only form actually replayed on confirmation (+0.002114, CI [+0.00161, +0.00262]). The '+0.00179 for st_p07 on confirmation' in the hypothesis is an exact estimate on the fixed ef graph, not a replay.

The placement in the hypothesis is wrong. The measured stitch_final_graph call runs AFTER linefit (and so after the short-track filter), after the edge filter and before divinsert. It does not run 'before the short-track filter and linefit'. Stitching before the short-track filter would rescue short tracks and change the node count (the node-multiplier trap). The FN report also says a pre-short-track stitch is worth little (only ~115 of 606 a_tail FN can be attached).
evidence.source: tools/build_probe_kernel.py lines 669-821 (STITCH_CALL anchored after the linefit / EDGEFILTER_CALL); l6_fn_anatomy_report.md section 4

evidence.claim: The stitch mostly repairs breaks that the edge filter creates. Breaks go from 150 to 399 after ef, 281 of them with an ILP edge. Without ef the stitch is worth only +0.0008 (exact estimate on exp39, 115 TP / 5 FP) and +0.00067 in the selection replay. Its value therefore depends on probe 29.

The stitch interacts with DaughterNet insertion (exp48), which has never been measured. The orphan branch of divinsert needs a daughter v with no incoming edge, which is exactly the track start the stitch consumes, and divinsert runs after the stitch. A stitched u also becomes a new single-child parent candidate. With steal on, a stitched edge with p < 0.3 can be stolen. The confirmation replay had no insertion (divisions 16/28/71, the same as exp39).

Break-even arithmetic holds. An added evaluable edge with precision p changes J by about [p*D - TP*(1-p)]/D^2, which is positive iff p > J/(1+J) ~ 0.48 at J ~ 0.93. Measured in-sample precision is 0.937 (281/300 on 199 videos), 0.949 on confirmation, and 0.79 for the p<0.7 slice. Unevaluable additions are free, and the node multiplier is unchanged.

Transfer risk is higher than the hypothesis says. The candidates are exactly the ILP links the relink rejected, with a median displacement of 10.6 um against a median true step of 1.8 um. These long, rare moves are where an edge net trained in-sample is least trustworthy. Relink-off, the global 'trust the ILP' change, lost 0.002 on the LB. The edge filter (probe 29) makes the same bet on ILP edges, so its LB result is the best available transfer evidence.

implementation_notes: CODE (already built, no new code needed): tools/build_probe_kernel.py --patch stitch; the replay keys are st.*. The call order is fixed: linefit -> edgefilter -> swapfix -> stitch -> divinsert, whatever order the patches are given in. The function keeps every node, adds only ILP edges (source has out-degree 0, target has in-degree 0, target at t+1), orders them by p descending, uses each node once, and flags each added edge with stitched=1 and edge_prob = the ILP p. There is no explicit fork test, and none is needed: u has no successor, so the stitch cannot create a fork. PITFALLS: (1) Keep the measured placement, after linefit. Do NOT move it before the short-track filter or linefit as the hypothesis says: that changes node counts (multiplier) and coordinates, and has no measurement behind it. (2) st_p07 fails the 44b6 mean gate (+0.00078 < +0.001). Ship st_all (STITCH_ENABLE=1, min_prob 0), which is the only replay-confirmed form; st_p06 (44b6 +0.00102) is the conservative fallback. Guess: st_all and st_p06 will differ by <= 0.0002 on the LB. (3) divinsert interaction: with steal, the stitched edges carry a finite p, so a stitched edge with p < 0.3 (steal_prob_max) can be stolen. That only happens with st_all (p05/p06 remove it). Orphan daughters consumed by the stitch drop out of insertion. Measure divins_added / divins_triples_orphan and division TP/FP with and without the stitch. (4) DaughterNet node p in the lab covers the candidate nodes of the exp39 graph (coords_exp39.parquet, 649,808 triples incl. the steal pool). On an ef/stitch graph, new triples may involve nodes without p, which are silently skipped. Report divins_missing_p per config. If it grows by more than about 5% relative to e48, re-export coords (--export-coords --export-base <cfg>) and rescore with kdn_score on a Kaggle GPU before trusting the division term. (5) Statistics: define a tie as |delta| < 1e-9. Count 44b6 wins and losses at the leak-group level (splits.json meta.leak_groups, group mean; ungrouped videos are singletons), not per video, because overlapping crops share GT edges. (6) Changing the gate after seeing the confirmation result is a post-hoc protocol change. Declare it as such in CONTEXT.md, apply it only to add-only rules, and do not use it to rescue other failed rules without re-checking them. The final arbiter is still the bundle probe. (7) The lab cache was built at tight gate 6.0; the kernel runs 5.5. The stitch candidate set depends on which ILP edges the relink rejected, so the kernel's set will differ a little from the lab's (as it did for ef, ~9.5%).
refined_change: (1) Gate fix, declared as a protocol amendment in CONTEXT.md. For add-only rules (no node change, no edge removal), replace '>= 55% of videos gain per embryo' with a tie-aware sign criterion. Drop exact ties (|d| < 1e-9); require wins/(wins+losses) >= 0.8 per embryo, with 44b6 counted per leak group (group mean delta) and at least 5 non-tied units per embryo. Keep the gates on overall delta (>= +0.002, or bundle-only below it), per-embryo mean >= +0.001, 90% CI lower bound > 0, and node ratio change <= 0.01%. Under this rule ef_st_all passes: 44b6 5/0 clusters, 6bba 46/0. (2) Ship the stitch ONLY if probe 29 shows the edge filter transfers, as part of the ef bundle: exp48 + --patch edgefilter (ALT=3, RELINK=1, PRUNE=1) + --patch stitch --set STITCH_ENABLE=1 (st_all, min_prob 0). The fallback is STITCH_MIN_PROB=0.6 if the lab shows a division-insertion conflict from low-p stitched edges. Keep the call where it is now: after linefit and ef, before divinsert. Not st_p07 (fails the 44b6 mean gate), and not before the short-track filter. (3) If probe 29 fails, drop the stitch: without ef it is worth ~+0.0007, below every gate and invisible on the LB.

Configs; the insertion params must match the lab's exp48 row, and cap 4 / alpha 1 / threshold 0.5 below are my assumption for the OOF equivalent of ensemble 0.4, so check them against CONTEXT: e48 = exp39,leaf_prune=0.3,insert=1,ins.steal=1,ins.cap_video=4,ins.alpha=1,ins.threshold=0.5 ; e48_ef = e48 + ef.alt=3,ef.relink=1,ef.prune=1 ; e48_ef_st = e48_ef + st.enable=1 ; e48_ef_st06 = e48_ef + st.min_prob=0.6 ; e48_st = e48 + st.enable=1 (no-ef fallback). Also add ef_st_all=exp39,ef.alt=3,ef.relink=1,ef.prune=1,st.enable=1 as a reproduction check: it must give 0.945094 on confirmation. Run 1 uses --control e48_ef; run 2 (a report-only rerun, tails cached) uses --control e48. Report per embryo: mean delta, 90% paired-bootstrap CI, W/L/T per video AND per 44b6 leak group, edge dTP/dFP, node ratio, division TP/FP/FN, divins_added, divins_triples_orphan and divins_missing_p. SUCCESS: e48_ef_st vs e48_ef confirmation delta >= +0.0015 with CI lower bound > 0; each embryo mean >= +0.001; tie-aware win share >= 0.8 on both embryos (44b6 by leak group, >= 5 non-tied units); node ratio change <= 0.01%; division TP not lower and division FP not higher than e48_ef (or net division delta >= -0.0002); divins_missing_p no more than 5% above e48. Runtime: tails for leaf_prune 0.3 are new (a base key change), so expect one full tail pass on 199 videos. Guess: ~1-2 h on 4 vCPU; the stitch and ef steps are seconds per video. No GPU is needed unless divins_missing_p grows, in which case re-export coords and rescore with kdn_score on a Kaggle T4 (~20-30 min, guess).

Without ef: ~+0.0007, not worth shipping. Public/private: +0.000..+0.002, conditional on probe 29 transferring. Best guess +0.001 at out-of-sample precision around 0.7.
